Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Title: Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation; Application for an Exemption From Grote Industries, LLC
Action: Notice of availability of supplemental information; request for comments.
Abstract: This notice advises the public of new information that FMCSA believes is relevant to the application from Grote Industries, LLC (Grote) for an exemption from the requirement that exterior lighting devices on commercial motor vehicles (CMVs) be steady-burning. If granted, the exemption would allow motor carriers to operate CMVs equipped with auxiliary warning lamps controlled by Grote's Rear-End Collision Warning (RCW) system. Following publication of the Agency's notice seeking comment, Grote provided additional information to FMCSA staff concerning the design and operation of the RCW system, including the color and activation sequence of the auxiliary warning lamps, the interaction between the RCW and brake-activated warning functions, system operation on combination vehicles, and the operation of the radar detection system. FMCSA is making this supplemental information available in the docket and provides an opportunity for public comment.
